owner.workstream: Path of Exile 2 controls and enforcement research

applicability.tool_id: Azeron; native weapon sets; software/hardware input helpers
applicability.context: User requests inference from ban patterns, shared factors and unshared factors; protection of the current PC remains the priority

symptom: Public ban reports conflate identity linkage, detection signals and restriction type; the exact detector and hardware enforcement are unknown

approach: Trace summaries to original posts and staff replies
Separate account bans, account locks, input-rate kicks, warnings, website failures and product-license HWID errors
Compare shared and unshared factors without treating correlation as causation
Mark PoE1 history, early PoE2 incidents and current policy distinctly
Do not count the same incident repeated by a relative, Reddit summary and forum opening as independent cases
limitations: Search-selected reports with unknown setups and missing denominators
No controlled counterfactual or authenticated account/enforcement records
Steam repeated-level-40 case remains indexed-search-only; direct open showed a content-preference gate
No original video watched, private Discord records accessed or game/software inspection
No timing threshold, blacklist key, detector signature or individual risk probability established

sources.observation: Staff acknowledge reports of potentially incorrect restrictions and efforts to fix/prevent recurrence.
sources.limit: No cause, exact level trigger, algorithm or hardware link disclosed.

sources.coverage: IP-issue acknowledgement and resolution replies read
sources.observation: Staff identify an IP-banning issue as separate from the opening account-ban issue and later report it should be resolved.
sources.limit: Historical incident, not proof of current routine punitive IP bans or hardware enforcement.

sources.coverage: Original reports and author's account-state update read
sources.observation: Reports cluster around the Act 3 generator boss at levels 38 and 40. Opening author later says two accounts show different ban states but is confused about their linking and which account was used.
sources.limit: Not an exact universal level-40 trigger or clean same-PC control. One referenced player's incident also appears in P04.

sources.coverage: Opening, staff reply and author/another user's restoration reports read
sources.observation: Author explicitly says the PC account is banned and posts using PSN. The author and another participant subsequently report being unbanned.
sources.limit: A Reddit summary labels this a console ban incorrectly; exclude it as console enforcement evidence. Forum access through PSN is not observed PS5 gameplay.

sources.revision: Indexed post/replies displayed June 10; exact year not verified
sources.coverage: Indexed original text read; direct opening returned content-preference gate
sources.observation: Player reports two different accounts banned near level 40 in Act 3 and mentions a VPN. They quote support permitting a new account.
sources.limit: PC/network/client/platform linking, behavior and timing were not independently controlled or verified; repeated bans do not isolate hardware.

sources.coverage: Same-PC and main/alt outcome text read; attachments not authenticated
sources.observation: Historical PoE1 reports describe an alt banned while a main on the same PC remained usable.
sources.limit: Weakens an unconditional all-accounts-on-PC explanation for those reports; does not exclude selective hardware correlation or establish current PoE2 protection.

sources.coverage: Opening and listed companion applications read
sources.observation: Player suspects G HUB after a third-party-software ban but also lists several other applications and a network-routing tool.
sources.limit: Title is a causal suspicion; no authenticated cause, isolated change or audited comparison population.

sources.observation: Warning persisted after companion-tool removal but reportedly disappeared after old filter/custom-sound files were removed. Game login remained possible.
sources.limit: Warning is a different outcome from a ban; removing multiple files does not isolate an exact signature or confirmed false-positive cause.

sources.coverage: Opening, gem-combination recovery claims and contrary later reports read
sources.observation: Players report action-rate kicks, immediate relogin and gem/build-related recovery. Some later reports say crashes persist without the suspected combination.
sources.limit: Kick is not an account ban or proof of macro use. Reported fixes are historical and not recommended as current configuration.

sources.revision: 2024-11-13 account-system announcement; current served FAQ reviewed 2026-10-12
sources.observation: Explicitly linked/associated sub-accounts share ban consequences under the published policy.
sources.limit: Do not extend to every independent account sharing a PC or IP; historical user confusion is not an exemption.

sources.coverage: Automatically collected gameplay data, anti-cheat/security data and platform identifiers read
sources.observation: Discloses account/platform IDs, IP, hardware/install/machine IDs, OS data, processes, memory/drivers, gameplay activity, quest timing, item acquisition and inventories.
sources.limit: Collection/purpose disclosure is not a verified implementation, scoring rule, component list or evidence that every signal automatically propagates bans.

sources.coverage: Keyboard-event flag and timestamp fields read
sources.observation: Windows exposes injected-event flags for low-level keyboard events.
sources.limit: Does not prove GGG observes these flags, treats them as violations or cannot identify externally generated gameplay behavior.

sources.observation: Native skill use can select an assigned equipped weapon set before using the skill.
sources.limit: A weapon-change/cast result alone is not proof of an external multi-input macro. Does not cover arbitrary inventory/gem loadouts.

sources.coverage: Author disclaimer and categorical no-IP-ban assertion read; no software used
sources.observation: Botting-community poster explicitly calls the guide personal opinion, declines safety guarantees and nevertheless asserts studios never IP-ban.
sources.limit: Categorical assertion is inconsistent with P02's documented historical IP-restriction incident. PoE1 botting opinion is not PoE2 detector evidence; evasion advice not adopted.

case_comparisons.outcome: Historical PoE2 account bans clustered around Act 3; restoration reports and staff acknowledgement of possible incorrect restrictions
case_comparisons.inference: Progression-linked processing or a historical error is compatible; exact universal level-40 enforcement is unsupported because levels 38 are also reported.
case_comparisons.confidence: Moderate for a reported cluster; low for its mechanism

case_comparisons.outcome: Two accounts reportedly banned near the same progression stage
case_comparisons.inference: Both renewed account/progression checks and persistent shared environment could explain it; hardware is not uniquely selected.

case_comparisons.outcome: PoE1 alt banned while main reportedly usable on same PC
case_comparisons.inference: An unconditional immediate machine-wide blacklist is a poor fit for those reported outcomes. Account-specific decisions or selective linkage remain possible.
case_comparisons.confidence: Moderate conditional inference; low for current PoE2

case_comparisons.outcome: Separate historical IP restriction acknowledged and reported resolved
case_comparisons.inference: Network restrictions can produce access loss independently of an account-ban incident; no hardware blacklist is required to explain this example.

case_comparisons.outcome: Peripheral-software suspicion and separate warning recovery after file removal
case_comparisons.inference: Local state is a candidate signal, but program name alone is not an established ban cause and warning recovery cannot be counted as a ban reversal.

case_comparisons.outcome: Gameplay-related kicks with immediate relogin; native use can also trigger weapon switching
case_comparisons.inference: Action sequences/rates require game context. Fast output or multiple visible effects do not identify how many physical inputs occurred or prove prohibited automation.
case_comparisons.confidence: Moderate engineering inference; actual server input telemetry unknown

linkage_matrix.unknown: How every independent-account case is handled
Identifier derivation, exact components, persistence, blacklist use and restriction scope

linkage_matrix.assessment: Disclosed security signal with one distinct historical restriction incident; shared IP alone does not uniquely identify a person or PC

linkage_matrix.factor: OS version, hardware model or peripheral brand
linkage_matrix.assessment: Environment descriptions are shared by many unrelated users; no case establishes them alone as a unique identifier or sufficient cause
linkage_matrix.unknown: Specific versions/configurations involved in any confirmed detector rule

linkage_matrix.assessment: Gameplay data is disclosed; pattern-based classification is technically compatible with reported outcomes
linkage_matrix.unknown: Features, thresholds, automation versus review, exact causation

linkage_matrix.assessment: General Windows capability affecting some input paths
linkage_matrix.unknown: Whether GGG uses it and how it distinguishes permitted remapping from prohibited automation

mechanism_hypotheses.claim: Account state and explicit platform linking

mechanism_hypotheses.state: Plausible from disclosed data and OS capability; exact GGG checks unknown
Plausible from disclosed gameplay records; implementation and thresholds unknown

mechanism_hypotheses.claim: Device correlation or selective device restrictions

mechanism_hypotheses.state: Historical IP incident confirmed; current general rule unknown

mechanism_hypotheses.claim: Progression-triggered review or historical restriction bug
mechanism_hypotheses.state: Fits historical cluster; neither exact trigger nor detector established

observation.claim: Original sources reveal several distinct restriction outcomes, near-38/40 Act 3 reports, restoration reports, documented linked-account policy and a separately acknowledged IP issue. Public accounts omit enough variables to prevent isolating a hardware cause.

inference.claim: A model with separate account, local-client, gameplay and network checks fits the evidence better than attributing all outcomes to a universal hardware blacklist. Device correlation remains technically possible. Recognition, evidence of a violation and choice of restriction are separate decisions; none gives a validated safe path for the proposed multi-input macro.
inference.confidence: Moderate for the explanatory model; unknown for GGG's architecture and any individual's ban probability

supported_next_action.capability: Continue evidence-based native weapon-set and manual-input/display helper design
success_evidence: Native weapon/skill assignment is already documented
Use actual character readback before any game configuration change

permission.current_request_reference: Pattern research and public-source analysis only; email remains an unsent draft

stop_conditions: Do not infer a safe delay or hardware immunity from surviving users
Do not use game bans, community bans, kicks, warnings and license errors interchangeably
Do not treat new account/Windows changes as a controlled isolated experiment

recovery.artifact_alias: Existing R2 profiles and v0.1 offline lab retained
recovery.rollback_procedure: Remove only this new record and its corresponding history entry; no runtime change

change_triggers: Original case outcome or cause verified
New controlled public comparison with independent outcome verification

next_boundary: Patterns identify plausible mechanisms and confounders, not stealth settings or protected hardware. No live anti-cheat/account test or email performed.
